summary:
The demo does not show the changed application executing the reviewed behavior. Every browser capture is a per-URL state render: each image is loaded from ".../?scenario=initial|request-changes-done|approve-done|github-failed|host-check|linear-failed|stale-head|unlinked|abandoned|replacement|identity-guard|checked-human". No `scenario` switch exists anywhere in the changed application source (rg over the whole candidate tree finds `scenario` only as a CSS class name in portal/bettaview/src/styles.css), so the temporary Worker that served these pages is a demo-only bundle that paints a chosen status panel rather than the app reaching that state. The images confirm this: in "request-changes-done" and "approve-done" the Comment button is still the selected review type, the thread count is 0, no draft, no reply and no composed body is ever visible, no Publish click or in-flight state is captured, the "stale-head" page still shows a green "Exact head 7e1ec3f" badge while the panel text claims the head changed, and "replacement" shows literal step labels "Replacement GitHub review"/"Replacement Linear · In Progress". That is a fixture screenshot, which the plan and the owner's 2026-09-20 instruction explicitly reject.

The provider evidence is partly real but mostly disconnected from the app. Three receipts (REQUEST_CHANGES 5260493456, APPROVE 5260494478, APPROVE 5260495532) carry hand-written bodies and the marker "<!-- bettaview:v1 sac182-attempt01a0be97-request-changes-v1 -->" style operation IDs, i.e. they were created by direct safe-adapter calls, not by the application's publish pipeline, which emits a base64 bundle marker (as the single app-path COMMENT receipt 5260523254 does). Real provider events produced outside the changed application do not prove the feature.

The one Showboat run does exercise real code (publishContinuation -> ReviewContinuationRpc -> continueReviewToLinear) and produces one genuine GitHub review, but its harness bypasses most of the claimed path: it runs on an in-memory SQLite D1 stand-in instead of the temporary Worker's D1 (so no publish_environment storage migration or SELECT read-back exists anywhere in the evidence), it monkey-patches globalThis.fetch so GitHub GET /user, the pull-request read, /files and /comments are fabricated and the create-review response (id, html_url) is synthesized locally, the live-head check is stubbed as `async () => config.head`, and the Linear move is an inline callback rather than the real workflow Linear client. It ends with linear_status "awaiting_delivery": no verified signed delivery row, no gate choice and no traversal is ever shown. The signed Linear deliveries in the provider files were never demonstrated arriving at the deployed ingress, being HMAC-verified, deduplicated by delivery key, or committing the gate choice, which is the central claim of the approved specs.

Finally, the evidence checklist marks all twelve scenarios complete while justifying s02, s06, s07, s08, s10, s11 and s12 with "passing tests cover ...". The owner said tests running is not proof and the plan's corrections exclude test output as evidence for any scenario; a checked box plus a test claim is not a demonstration. Separately, all evidence was captured on treeSha 14010894c71d7e7b61b9ef83cdb023596e795bd8 while the subject under review is treeSha c784f73af4e362fed975a20be5dea2e075584630, so the captures should be re-taken on the reviewed tree.

To fix: serve the real BettaView + ReviewContinuation bundle on the publish_environment Worker with its D1 binding, prepare run/gate/account rows server-side (not by URL parameter), drive each scenario by actually composing drafts and clicking Publish/Retry in Chromium, and pair each capture with real storage read-back (SELECT over project_bettaview_accounts, review_intents, review_parts, review_attempts, review_continuation_leases, the Linear ingress row with signature_verified and delivery_key, the gate choice and traversal rows) plus provider read-back of the pull request whose review body carries the app's own bundle marker. Keep synthetic faults confined to the real service's outbound transport and label them.

scenarios.reason: Only one capture exists, taken from /settings?scenario=settings, showing an already-connected account at policy version 2. The plan's sequence is missing entirely: no zero-row SELECT before the demo, no disconnected state, no connection form populated by trusted Access/GitHub/Linear reads, no save action, no SELECT over project_bettaview_accounts or bettaview_account_audit, no run allocation freezing the three IDs plus the policy version, no proof that version 1 stayed immutable while an allocated run kept version 1, and no rejected mismatched-identity connection. The panel also prints the Linear issue UUID 0ea73e5f-837c-4af1-9c8b-c11216146bae as the Linear user ID, which matches the hand-prepared fixture data rather than a trusted provider read.

The cited image is the ?scenario=initial render with zero threads and no draft; no inline note or reply is ever written, no autosave indicator is shown, and no reload-restores-drafts capture exists. Nothing demonstrates the absence of provider writes: no adapter listing showing zero reviews/comments for the review ID, no Linear read showing the issue still in Human Review, no SELECT proving no intent, lease or part rows, and no network/storage inspection proving the browser holds no Linear credential and makes no linear.app request. The checklist backs this with passing BettaView tests, which the plan excludes as evidence.

The 'both steps done' image is loaded from ?scenario=request-changes-done and still shows Comment as the selected review type with zero threads, so no REQUEST_CHANGES selection, reply composition or Publish click was demonstrated. The matching GitHub receipt 5260493456 carries a hand-written body and the marker 'bettaview:v1 sac182-attempt01a0be97-request-changes-v1', not the app's base64 bundle marker, so it was created by a direct adapter call rather than through the publish pipeline. The Showboat run that does use the real RPC publishes a COMMENT review on an in-memory SQLite D1 with GitHub /user, pull, files and comments responses faked and the create-review response synthesized, and it ends at linear_status 'awaiting_delivery'. Missing: the signed Linear delivery verified at the deployed ingress with its delivery key and ack time, the gate choice recording the saved review as the human act, exactly one edit-edge traversal, lease release, and the idempotent resend producing no new rows or provider records.

The 'approve-done' image is again a URL-selected render with Comment still highlighted and no inline notes anywhere on the page. Receipt 5260494478 was produced by a direct adapter call (body text 'BettaView isolated provider proof: approval with review notes...', marker 'sac182-attempt01a0be97-approve-notes-v1') rather than by the app, and no inline comment records are shown at all. Missing: the two composed notes and APPROVE selection in the UI, publication through the app, the two inline comments with item markers read back from GitHub, the D1 row for the signed Merging delivery, exactly one traversal on the trusted merge edge with no edit traversal, and the adapter read proving BettaView merged nothing.

This scenario reuses the identical ?scenario=approve-done image as s04, so no distinct run was observed; the shared capture cannot show that a no-notes approval was submitted. The paired receipt 5260495532 again carries a hand-written proof body and an operation-ID marker, so it is an adapter-created review, not an app publication. Missing: a capture of APPROVE selected with zero notes before publishing, the app-generated review on the live head with zero new inline comments for that review ID, and the Merging delivery plus single merge traversal read from D1.

The single ?scenario=github-failed image paints 'Failed Retryable' and the text 'github_rejected' without any preceding publish attempt, and the failure source is neither a real GitHub 422 nor a labelled transport injection that is visible in the evidence. Missing: proof that the task stayed in Human Review (adapter read), the provider-operation/fault SELECT showing the original provider message and cause chain stored write-once with the matching safe code and no secret column, the lease never upgraded to the Linear phase, and the in-scenario recovery (edit to COMMENT, republish) showing exactly one review on the pull request plus separate append-only attempt rows. The checklist substitutes passing workflow tests, which the plan excludes.

Only the phase-B end state is present, as a ?scenario=host-check render. Phase A is entirely absent: no dropped-response publish, no reconciliation read-back adopting the existing host record ID, and no follow-on 'both steps done' capture. No provider listing proves exactly one review and one inline note after the lost response, and no review_attempts/review_parts SELECT shows a single generation with an adopted host record ID. For phase B there is no ops-item row, no retained lease and no adapter read proving the issue never moved. The checklist again leans on idempotency tests, which are not accepted evidence here.

The one ?scenario=linear-failed image shows GitHub done and Linear 'Failed Retryable' with a Retry button, but the retry is never clicked and no after state is captured, so the central claim that a retry moves only the task and never republishes to GitHub is undemonstrated. The whole delivery-gap phase (shortened labelled deadline, awaiting-delivery state, escalation to host check, one ops item, no second mutation) has no evidence at all. Missing storage proof throughout: the unmodified GraphQL cause chain, a new generation limited to the Linear scope, the HMAC-verified and delivery-key-deduplicated ingress row, the gate choice and the single traversal.

The stale-head capture is contradictory proof of a URL-selected state: the page still displays the green 'Exact head 7e1ec3f' badge while the injected panel says the head changed, and no draft content is visible even though the scenario turns on drafts staying readable. No adapter output shows a new commit advancing the head, no attempted Publish is captured, no SELECT shows the absent part receipt, absent lease upgrade and the recorded stale-head rule fault, and the reload-then-publish-against-head-B half of the scenario is missing entirely. The unlinked capture is likewise a canned render with no SELECT proving no intent row was created.

The 'abandoned' and 'replacement' captures are two more URL-selected renders; the replacement panel even uses literal labels 'Replacement GitHub review' and 'Replacement Linear · In Progress' instead of app state. Nothing shows the reply actually published during a labelled pause, the head advancing to B, the intent terminalising with the published reply URL and the unpublished item list, the lease released with no Linear operation, or the replacement view suppressing the already published reply. No provider listing proves one reply, zero reviews for the abandoned intent and exactly one review pinned to head B, and no review_parts rows show the prior receipt or the supersedes link.

The scenario's whole point is four real authenticated requests to the deployed app (second review ID on an open gate, forged page identity, mismatched frozen GitHub user ID, reused review ID with changed bound facts) and their rejection responses plus lease, permit, fault and provider counts. None of those requests or responses appear in the evidence. The single ?scenario=identity-guard image is a canned blocked state, and the checklist justifies the rest with passing service and orchestration tests, which the plan excludes as proof.

This is the requirement that only a checked human act can move the gate, and it is the least demonstrated. There is no app-actor Linear state change delivered to the deployed ingress, no verified delivery row, no SELECT showing the event stored for audit with the run still awaiting human approval and no gate choice, no adapter read showing Human Review restored exactly once, and no repetition test showing the repair is not endless. The cited ?scenario=checked-human image is a canned waiting state, and the Showboat run never reaches a gate choice because it stops at linear_status 'awaiting_delivery'.
